title: Investor Data Room Checklist: What Belongs in Every Folder
summary: An investor data room checklist, folder by folder. See the documents a priced round asks for, which gaps stall diligence, and when to start building.
body_markdown:
## What a data room is and when to start building one


The term sheet is signed and the lead’s associate emails over a request list. That is the wrong week to start an investor data room checklist.


A fundraising data room is a permissioned repository holding the primary-source documents behind every claim in your pitch deck. The deck asserts. The data room substantiates. Six folders, roughly 45 to 70 documents at Series A, with three years plus year to date of history on anything financial or tax. Teams at indinero build the financial half of that room as a byproduct of the monthly close, which is why this section starts with timing instead of the list.


Have the room prepared before you officially kick off the raise. Andreessen Horowitz’s[insider’s guide to data rooms](https://a16z.com/the-insiders-guide-to-data-rooms-what-to-know-before-you-raise/) treats the room as a work in progress that evolves as investors ask questions. It names five items as the first-conversation core set: the deck, the cap table, historical P&L and burn, usage data covering growth and retention, and LTV to CAC with a payback period. Y Combinator’s[Series A diligence checklist](https://www.ycombinator.com/library/3h-series-a-diligence-checklist) , compiled by YC Continuity general counsel Jason Kwon, frames the room as a pre-term-sheet asset rather than a post-term-sheet chore. The stated payoff is a week off the closing process when everything sits in one place before the term sheet is signed.


Build four to six weeks before outreach. The window isn’t arbitrary. It’s set by the longest-lead items in the room, and three of them run on clocks you don’t control.


- **Accrual conversion.** If the books are cash basis, rebuilding three years under ASC 606 is a reconstruction project, not a toggle. ASC 606 has applied to private companies for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2019 under FASB ASU 2020-05, so there’s no early-stage exemption to claim at a priced round.
- **A fresh 409A.** Treasury Regulation 1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B)(2) gives an independent appraisal a presumption of reasonableness for 12 months from the valuation date, absent a material event, under[26 CFR 1.409A-1](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/section-1.409A-1) . An appraisal engagement plus board ratification is a multi-week item.
- **State registrations.** A missing payroll withholding or unemployment insurance account has to be opened with the state. That’s agency turnaround time, not founder effort.


One more item belongs in that window, and it postdates most checklists on the subject. The National Venture Capital Association updated its model documents on October 2, 2025, and the practitioner read from[Foley and Lardner](https://www.foley.com/insights/publications/2025/10/breaking-down-the-nvca-what-founders-and-vcs-need-to-know/) recommends a regulatory health check two to four weeks before fundraising. That check covers Outbound Investment Security Program and Data Security Program exposure, data flow diagrams and vendor inventories, cap table beneficial ownership validation, and a QSBS eligibility memorandum.


How much of the full list applies depends on the round.


- **Pre-seed and seed.** The a16z core five, plus incorporation documents and a simple cap table. Roughly 12 to 20 files.
- **Series A.** All six folders populated, three years plus year to date of financial and tax history, the model, top customer contracts, and IP assignments for every founder and employee. Roughly 45 to 70 files.
- **Series B and later.** Add reviewed or audited statements, a SOC 2 Type 2 report, multi-state registration evidence by state, and a deferred revenue waterfall tied to the general ledger.


A fundraising data room is also not the same exercise as a sale process. If you’re preparing for an acquirer rather than a lead investor,[financial due diligence](https://www.indinero.com/blog/financial-due-diligence/) covers the buyer-side analytical review, and[what investors expect from Series A accounting](https://www.indinero.com/blog/series-a-accounting/) covers the books underneath all of it.


## The checklist, folder by folder


Number the folders and lock the naming convention before you upload anything. Diligence teams work from their own request list and tick items off, so numbered folders let an associate map your tree onto their list in one pass.


Use` 01_Corporate` through` 06_Product_IP_Security` , dates in filenames as` YYYYMMDD` , and a version number on anything that will be replaced. A room survives three rounds of document swaps only if nobody has to guess which file is current.


Three columns matter for every document, and this is where most published checklists stop short. The document name is the easy part. The **history period expected** and the **format** are what decide whether an associate can work with the file or has to email you about it. Three years plus year to date on financials and returns. Trailing 12 months of reconciliations. The last 24 months of 409A reports. Top 10 customer contracts by ARR. Live XLSX for anything with a formula in it.


Set a materiality threshold too. YC’s checklist puts the bar for material agreements at obligations or payments above $25,000, which is a reasonable default for what gets uploaded until the lead’s request list names a different number.


One more file earns its place at the top. A` 00_Start_Here` document holding the cap table summary, a one-page financial summary, and a two-paragraph index of the room is worth more than any single document inside it. If your round will also pull an audit into view,[audit prep for startups](https://www.indinero.com/blog/audit-prep-for-startups-checklist/) covers the overlap between the two document sets.


### Corporate and governance


This folder proves the company exists, is in good standing, and has validly issued every share and option on the cap table. The diligence team is testing for an unbroken chain of authorizations. Every grant, every pool increase, and every financing needs a board or stockholder action behind it, dated correctly.


Document History expected Format


Certificate of Incorporation plus every amendment and restatement, as filed Since formation PDF, state-stamped copies


Bylaws, as currently amended Current PDF


Certificates of Designation, if a series was created outside a restated charter Since formation PDF


Board minutes and written board consents Since formation, complete and gap-free PDF, one file per meeting or consent, dated


Stockholder minutes and written stockholder consents Since formation PDF


Certificate of Good Standing from the state of incorporation Dated within 30 days of the raise PDF


Foreign qualification certificates for every state the company is qualified in Current PDF by state


Prior financing documents, including each round’s stock purchase agreement, investors’ rights agreement, voting agreement, and right of first refusal and co-sale agreement All prior rounds PDF


Outstanding SAFEs and convertible notes, signed, with a conversion schedule All outstanding PDF plus one XLSX schedule


Form D filings and state blue sky notice filings All prior rounds PDF or EDGAR links


Management rights letters and indemnification agreements All outstanding PDF


Subsidiary formation documents and intercompany agreements Since formation PDF


The[NVCA model legal documents](https://nvca.org/model-legal-documents/) set the vocabulary for this folder. As of October 2026 the current versions are the Certificate of Incorporation, Stock Purchase Agreement, and Investors’ Rights Agreement updated October 2025, the Voting Agreement updated June 2026, the Right of First Refusal and Co-Sale Agreement updated April 2026, the Management Rights Letter and Indemnification Agreement from July 2020, and the Model Legal Opinion. If a prior round used NVCA forms, label your files with the NVCA names. Counsel on the other side will find them faster.


Two items in this folder are cheap to fix now and awkward to explain later. Form D is due within 15 days after the first sale of securities, filed on EDGAR at no fee, and it’s what puts state regulators on notice for blue sky purposes, per the SEC’s guidance on[what Form D is](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/what-form-d) . Good standing is the other one. Delaware corporations owe an annual franchise tax report and payment by March 1, and the state assesses a $200 penalty plus interest at 1.5% per month, will not issue a Certificate of Good Standing while a report or tax is outstanding, and voids the charter after more than a year of nonpayment. Investors routinely make a current good standing certificate a closing condition.


### Financial statements and the model


This folder is the one that gets read first and hardest. The diligence team is testing whether the revenue number in the deck appears in the accounting records, and whether the forward model is consistent with the trailing twelve months.


Document History expected Format


Income statement, balance sheet, and statement of cash flows, GAAP accrual basis 3 fiscal years plus YTD, monthly and annual views XLSX for monthly detail, PDF of annual statements


Trial balance and general ledger detail Same 3 years plus YTD XLSX or CSV export


Monthly close package with bank and credit card reconciliations Trailing 12 months minimum, 24 preferred PDF per month


Accounts receivable aging Most recent close plus trailing 12 monthly snapshots XLSX


Accounts payable aging and accrued liabilities schedule Most recent close XLSX


Deferred revenue waterfall reconciling bookings to billings to GAAP revenue 3 years plus YTD, monthly XLSX, one tab


Revenue recognition policy memo under ASC 606, with the five-step analysis applied to your actual contract types Current PDF or DOCX


Lease schedule and ASC 842 right-of-use asset and liability rollforward Current plus prior year XLSX


Capitalized software and fixed asset register with depreciation schedules Since inception of the policy XLSX


Debt and venture debt agreements with amortization schedules and covenant compliance certificates All outstanding PDF plus XLSX


The financial model, monthly for 24 to 36 months then annual through year five Forward looking, prior-period actuals locked XLSX, formulas live, no hardcoded outputs


SaaS metrics pack covering ARR, net and gross revenue retention, logo retention, CAC, CAC payback, gross margin, burn, and runway Trailing 24 months, monthly XLSX, every metric traceable to the GL


Bank statements for every operating and reserve account Trailing 12 months PDF


Reviewed or audited financial statements and the auditor’s report, if any exist Most recent 1 to 2 fiscal years PDF


Management letter or control deficiency list from any review or audit Most recent PDF


The metrics pack has to tie to the general ledger, and that single detail does more work than anything else in the folder. ARR in the deck, ARR in the model, and GAAP revenue in the statements are three different numbers by construction. The diligence team’s first move is to bridge them. A page in the room that shows the bridge preempts the question. An investor who has to build it alone assumes the worst about the gap.


Label the assurance level honestly. AICPA Statements on Standards for Accounting and Review Services, introduced by SSARS No. 21 in October 2014, define preparation, compilation, and review as distinct service levels. A compilation provides no assurance. A review provides limited assurance through inquiry and analytical procedures. An audit provides reasonable assurance and requires testing, internal control evaluation, and auditor independence. Most Series A rounds accept management-prepared accrual statements. Calling compiled statements audited is a disclosure problem, not a wording preference.


Deliver the model as a live XLSX, never a PDF. For how the model itself gets built, see the[Series A financial model template](https://www.indinero.com/blog/series-a-financial-model-template/) and the broader[financial modeling](https://www.indinero.com/blog/financial-modeling/) walkthrough. This page stops at naming the file.


### Tax filings and compliance


Tax is where exposure hides, and it’s the folder most founders underbuild. The diligence team is testing for unfiled returns, unregistered states, and positions taken without documentation behind them.


Document History expected Format


Federal income tax returns, Form 1120 with all schedules and statements, as filed 3 years PDF


State income and franchise tax returns, every state filed in 3 years, by state PDF, one subfolder per state


Delaware annual franchise tax reports and payment confirmations 3 years PDF


State sales and use tax registrations, permits, and returns 3 years of returns where registered PDF plus one XLSX registration matrix


Nexus study or nexus matrix showing sales and economic nexus by state against each state’s threshold Current, dated XLSX


State payroll registrations, income tax withholding and unemployment insurance accounts, by state Current, by state PDF plus the registration matrix


Quarterly payroll tax returns, Form 941, and annual Form 940 3 years PDF


State quarterly wage and unemployment reports 3 years, by state PDF


Forms W-2 and W-3, Forms 1099-NEC and 1096 3 years PDF


R&D credit study and Form 6765 as filed, with qualified research expense workpapers Every year claimed PDF plus XLSX workpapers


Section 174A domestic research expensing position and the foreign R&E 15-year amortization schedule Tax years beginning after December 31, 2024 XLSX plus a position memo


QSBS eligibility memorandum with aggregate gross assets history, redemption and repurchase logs, and original-issue records Since incorporation PDF plus XLSX


IRS and state notices, audit correspondence, and resolution documentation All open, plus closed within 3 years PDF


Tax basis schedules and NOL carryforward schedule with Section 382 analysis if ownership has shifted Since inception XLSX


The R&D position changed recently enough that stale workpapers now read as a gap. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, enacted July 4, 2025, added Section 174A and restored immediate expensing of domestic research and experimental expenditures for tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, permanently and with no sunset. Foreign R&E stays on 15-year amortization, Section 41(d) was revised to tie credit eligibility to amounts treated as domestic R&E under Section 174A, and the IRS has revised Form 6765 to require project-level detail. Put the position memo in the folder next to the return.


QSBS now sits here too, and that’s new. Following the October 2025 NVCA updates, investors ask for aggregate gross assets history since incorporation, redemption logs, and original-issue records to confirm Section 1202 eligibility. The gross assets threshold rose from $50 million to $75 million for stock issued after July 4, 2025, with tiered gain exclusions of 50%, 75%, and 100% at the three, four, and five year marks. Aggregate gross assets means cash plus the adjusted tax basis of tangible assets, and the burden of proof sits with the taxpayer. A priced round is the last clean moment to build that record.


### Customers, contracts, and revenue


This folder re-rates the revenue. Contracted ARR and cancelable ARR are not the same asset, and the diligence team will price the difference.


Document History expected Format


Top 10 customer contracts by ARR, fully executed with every amendment, order form, and statement of work Current and in force PDF, one subfolder per customer


Customer concentration analysis covering top 1, top 5, top 10, and top 25 as a percentage of revenue 3 years plus YTD XLSX


Standard MSA template and the standard order form or subscription agreement Current version plus version history DOCX redline plus PDF


Contract deviation log naming every customer whose terms differ from the template, with the specific deviation Current XLSX


Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Data Processing Addendum, and Acceptable Use Policy Current plus effective dates PDF or live URLs


Revenue by customer and by month 3 years plus YTD XLSX


Cohort retention analysis, logo retention and net revenue retention by signup cohort Trailing 24 to 36 months XLSX


Churned and downgraded accounts with stated reasons Trailing 24 months XLSX


Pipeline report and weighted forecast tied to the model’s revenue build Current XLSX


Reseller, channel, and referral partner agreements All in force PDF


Vendor and supplier agreements above the materiality threshold All in force PDF


Customer reference list with names, titles, and contact permission status Current XLSX, withheld until a term sheet


A diligence team reads the top 10 contracts for term length, renewal and auto-renewal mechanics, exclusivity, termination for convenience, most favored nation clauses, and assignment and change of control provisions. Commercial practice treats top five customers above 40% of revenue, or top 10 above 60%, as concentration that needs pricing or structural treatment. Three customers above 35% triggers stress testing.


Put the concentration table in the room yourself, with the churn-scenario math already done. The alternative is an associate doing that math without context.


Then flag cancelability in its own column. A contract that lets the customer walk on 30 days notice isn’t contracted revenue the way a 36-month non-cancelable subscription is. If your retention and ARR reporting isn’t built yet, the[SaaS metrics dashboard essentials](https://www.indinero.com/blog/saas-metrics-dashboard-essentials/) guide covers the definitions investors will hold you to.


### People, equity, and payroll


This folder answers two questions. Does the cap table tie to the stock ledger, and does the company own the work its people produced.


Document History expected Format


Cap table as of today, fully diluted, reconciled to the stock ledger with a tie-out column Current, dated XLSX


Stock ledger with every issuance, transfer, repurchase, and cancellation Since formation XLSX or platform export


Equity incentive plan documents, all amendments, and board and stockholder approvals for every pool increase Since adoption PDF


Option grant agreements plus the full grant log with grant date, board approval date, strike price, vesting commencement, vesting schedule, and exercise status Every grant, outstanding and exercised PDF per grant plus one XLSX log


Warrants, restricted stock purchase agreements, and RSU agreements All outstanding PDF


409A valuation reports Last 24 months, plus any refresh triggered by a material event PDF


Section 83(b) elections with proof of timely filing Every restricted stock holder PDF, including the mailing receipt


Founder stock purchase agreements with vesting and acceleration terms All founders PDF


Offer letters, employment agreements, and confidential information and invention assignment agreements Every current employee and every departure in the last 3 years PDF


Independent contractor and consulting agreements with IP assignment and work-for-hire language All in force plus 3 years of terminated PDF


Contractor classification analysis for every 1099 worker against the IRS common law factors Current XLSX plus a position memo


Organizational chart, current and projected post-funding Current PDF, withheld until a term sheet


Compensation table by role with base, bonus, and equity Current XLSX, withheld until a term sheet


Employee handbook and at-will acknowledgments Current PDF


Benefit plan documents and any 401(k) plan audit or Form 5500 Current plus 3 years of 5500s PDF


Non-compete, non-solicit, and separation agreements All in force PDF


Two years of 409A reports, not one. A single current report proves the strike price on grants issued today. Two reports with no gap between their coverage windows prove the strike price on every grant across the period an investor will actually test. When an appraisal qualifies under the safe harbor at Treasury Regulation 1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B)(2), the IRS bears the burden of showing the valuation was grossly unreasonable rather than the company bearing the burden of proving it correct. One report with a nine month hole behind it is a finding. For how the ledger and the table are supposed to reconcile, the[startup cap table](https://www.indinero.com/blog/startup-captable/) guide covers the mechanics.


The 83(b) item is where diligence actually breaks. The election must be filed with the IRS within 30 days of the issuance date, with no extensions and no equitable exceptions. Every restricted stock holder needs a copy plus proof of timely mailing in this folder.


Classification is the other live item. The IRS applies common law rules across behavioral control, financial control, and the type of relationship, with no set number of factors controlling the outcome, and Form SS-8 exists for genuinely unclear cases ([IRS guidance on contractor versus employee status](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/independent-contractor-self-employed-or-employee) ). On the labor side the picture is mid-rewrite. The Department of Labor stopped enforcing the 2024 independent contractor rule in May 2025 through Field Assistance Bulletin 2025-1, and on February 26, 2026 the Wage and Hour Division proposed rescinding it in favor of a two-core-factor economic reality test built on control and opportunity for profit or loss. Federal uncertainty doesn’t reduce the risk, because several states apply stricter tests and state law governs independently.


### Product, IP, and security


The diligence question here is ownership and exposure. Who owns the code, what license obligations came in with the dependencies, and where does customer data actually sit.


Document History expected Format


IP assignment agreements for every founder, employee, and contractor who has touched the product Since formation, no gaps PDF per person


Patent applications, issued patents, and prosecution status All filed PDF plus one XLSX docket


Trademark registrations and applications by class and jurisdiction All filed PDF plus XLSX


Domain name registrations and the registrar account of record All owned XLSX


Inbound software licenses plus a third-party and open-source dependency inventory with license type per package Current XLSX, generated from the SBOM


Outbound license agreements and any IP licensed out All in force PDF


University, government, or prior-employer IP encumbrances and releases All applicable PDF


Product roadmap and release history Current plus trailing 12 months PDF or XLSX


Architecture overview and data flow diagrams showing where customer data lives and which processors touch it Current PDF


SOC 2 Type 2 report, the Type 1 report, or the readiness and gap assessment with a dated remediation plan Most recent plus the prior period PDF, withheld until a term sheet or shared under NDA


Penetration test report and the remediation log Most recent PDF, withheld until a term sheet


Information security policy set covering access control, incident response, business continuity, and vendor management Current, with review dates PDF


Security incident and breach log Trailing 3 years PDF or XLSX


GDPR and CCPA compliance documentation, records of processing, and the subprocessor list Current PDF


Cyber liability, E&O, D&O, and general liability policies with declarations pages Current plus prior year PDF


Government customer contracts and federal contractor status documentation All in force PDF


SOC 2 deserves a realistic clock. The AICPA Trust Services Criteria define five categories, Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy, and Security is the Common Criteria that appears in every report. A Type 1 assesses control design at a point in time. A Type 2 assesses operating effectiveness across a period, typically three to twelve months. From a standing start, readiness runs three to six months, the observation window adds six to twelve, and fieldwork plus reporting adds four to six weeks. That’s nine to eighteen months end to end, far longer than a raise. For a company without a report, the correct artifact is the gap assessment plus a dated remediation plan, not silence.


The 2026 addition most checklists miss also lands in this folder. The model Stock Purchase Agreement now carries two-way representations on national security compliance, with both company and investor confirming no covered activity under the Outbound Investment Security Program, effective January 2, 2025, and no covered person status under the Data Security Program, effective April 8, 2025. The follow-up questions are specific. Foreign subsidiaries, contractors, board observers, and data arrangements touching countries of concern. Compute resources and AI training workflows running on foreign cloud or GPU providers. Data categories including biometric, genomic, geolocation, and health with third-party processor access. Government customer and federal contractor exposure. Data flow diagrams and a vendor inventory belong here for that reason, not only for privacy law.


## What investors open first


The cap table opens first, then historical P&L and burn. Before modeling your business, the fund models its own ownership.


1. **The cap table.** It decides whether the round math works at all, what post-money ownership looks like after the pool refresh, and whether the SAFE and note stack converts into something the lead can live with. It’s also the fastest document in the room to find a problem in.
2. **Historical P&L and burn.** The a16z core five puts this immediately after the cap table, specifically the path from gross revenue through net income to cash outflow. The question is simple. Does the revenue number in the deck appear in the accounting records.
3. **The metrics pack and retention cohorts.** ARR, net revenue retention, and CAC payback are where the thesis lives or dies. These get read against the P&L, not instead of it.
4. **The model.** Read after the actuals, as a test of judgment. The team checks whether forward assumptions are consistent with the trailing twelve months they just finished reading.
5. **Customer contracts and concentration.** Now the revenue gets re-rated for cancelability and concentration.
6. **Corporate, tax, people, and IP.** Legal diligence, usually run by outside counsel, frequently in parallel and often after the term sheet.


Why that order, stated plainly. The deck is an argument and the books are evidence. Everything in a pitch is a claim you chose to make. The general ledger is a record you didn’t get to curate.


The first hour is spent testing whether the two agree, and the answer sets the tone for everything after it. A gap found in hour one turns every later document into a search for more gaps.


Attention at the top of the funnel is also short. Dropbox’s[DocSend pitch deck research](https://www.dropbox.com/resources/docsend-pitch-deck-research) found investors spent over four minutes on decks that successfully raised and only a minute and a half on decks that did not, with average review time under three minutes. Short attention concentrated on evidence of a working business is exactly what the financials folder is for. Put the three first-read items where a tired associate finds them in one click, and make sure your burn reporting matches the statements behind it. The[burn rate and runway](https://www.indinero.com/blog/burn-rate-vs-runway-explained/) definitions are worth settling before an investor sets them for you.


## The gaps that stall a round


Seven gaps account for most stalled diligence, and six of them have a known fix and a known clock. Start the longest one today.


1. **Cash-basis books that need accrual conversion.** In diligence this shows up as revenue recognized on cash receipt, no deferred revenue balance, and annual prepaid contracts booked entirely in the month collected. The fix is a rebuild of three years plus year to date on an accrual basis under ASC 606, a deferred revenue waterfall, a re-derived balance sheet, and a policy memo applying the five-step model to your actual contract types. Lead time is four to eight weeks, longer when contract documentation is incomplete, because the recognition analysis means reading the contracts.
2. **Missing state tax registrations.** Revenue in 30 states, sales tax registrations in three. Employees in six states, withholding accounts in four. Sales and use tax follows economic nexus, and since South Dakota v. Wayfair in June 2018 states can require collection on economic activity alone, with thresholds typically at $100,000 but California, Texas, and New York at $500,000. At least 15 states had dropped the transaction count entirely as of July 1, 2025. Payroll is harsher, with an effectively zero-dollar threshold, so one remote employee triggers registration, withholding, quarterly returns, unemployment contributions, and new hire reporting. Lead time is two to six weeks per state, plus a voluntary disclosure agreement where back exposure exists.
3. **A stale 409A.** The most recent report is 14 months old, or it predates a financing, a material contract win, or a restructuring. The fix is a fresh independent appraisal, board ratification of the new fair market value, and documentation of the triggering event. Lead time is two to four weeks plus the board cycle. Grants issued against a stale valuation can’t be unwound, which makes late discovery a disclosure plus a tax exposure for every affected holder.
4. **Contractor classification.** A roster of long-tenured 1099 engineers with company email, company equipment, set hours, and no other clients. The fix is running every relationship against the IRS common law factors, reclassifying the ones that fail, and papering the rest with real contractor agreements carrying IP assignment language. Lead time is two to four weeks for the analysis, one payroll cycle to reclassify, and potentially months to resolve back payroll tax exposure. Check IP at the same time, because a contractor without a signed assignment may own code in your product.
5. **Unsigned and non-standard contracts.** Order forms with no countersignature, MSAs referencing exhibits that don’t exist, amendments agreed by email and never executed. The fix is a contract audit against the revenue by customer report, chasing countersignatures, confirmatory amendments where terms drifted, and a deviation log that discloses the differences instead of hiding them. Lead time is three to six weeks, because it depends on customer countersignature turnaround you don’t control. This one has the longest external dependency on the list.
6. **Incomplete corporate records.** A board consent approving a grant that postdates the grant date, minutes missing for two years, a pool increase with no stockholder approval, a lapsed franchise tax filing blocking good standing. The fix is reconstruction and ratification, with counsel drafting omnibus ratifying consents and the franchise tax brought current. Lead time is two to four weeks, faster when the gaps are documentary rather than substantive.
7. **Missing 83(b) elections.** There is no fix. The 30-day window admits no extensions and no equitable exceptions, so the only response is accurate disclosure, a tax analysis for the affected holder, and sometimes a negotiated indemnity.


That last one is the reason a checklist like this is worth reading months before a raise rather than during one. Six gaps have a clock. One has no door.


If the round is already moving and the finance work hasn’t started,[CFO support through a fundraise](https://www.indinero.com/blog/cfo-support-for-fundraising/) covers what gets triaged first.


## Access, permissions, and what to leave out


Give every fund its own named user account, never a shared link and never a shared password. Named accounts are what make the activity log mean anything.


Use folder-level and document-level permissioning so one room serves a first meeting and a confirmatory diligence without being rebuilt. Purpose-built platforms support this directly. Ansarada, for example, documents access control down to the individual document with role-based restrictions on viewing, editing, printing, and downloading.


- **Watermarking.** Apply a dynamic watermark carrying the viewer’s email, timestamp, and IP address to every document in the sensitive tiers. A static company watermark deters nothing. A watermark naming the viewer deters forwarding, which is the actual threat, because the realistic leak path is a partner forwarding a file to an operating advisor who happens to advise a competitor.
- **View-only versus download.** Default to view-only in the sensitive tiers and allow download on the items an investor genuinely has to work in. The model is the standard exception. Platform controls here include disabling downloads, setting expiry on individual documents, and expiring documents that have already been saved externally.
- **Activity logs.** The log is a sales instrument, not only a compliance record. File views, downloads, access location, and time on page tell you which fund read the cohort analysis and which one opened the deck once and never came back.
- **Instant revocation.** When a process goes dead, revoke access that week. Leaving a passed fund with live access to a room you’re still updating means your current metrics keep flowing to a firm with no economic reason to protect them.


Now the harder question, because the advice genuinely conflicts. Maximalist checklists say upload everything. a16z explicitly advises leaving out organizational charts and team bios, detailed three to five year projections, tax returns, audits, legal documents, board minutes, and market sizing analysis unless specifically requested. That’s a venture fund telling founders a first-meeting room should be smaller than most checklists suggest.


The resolution is tiering, not omission. Build the full room, then gate it.


- **Tier 1, open at the first substantive meeting.** Deck, cap table summary, historical P&L and burn, metrics pack, cohort retention, product overview.
- **Tier 2, open on a second or third meeting under NDA.** Full GAAP statements, the live model, the deferred revenue waterfall, anonymized top customer economics, architecture overview, the standard MSA template.
- **Tier 3, hold until a term sheet is signed.** Named customer contracts and the reference list with contact details. Per-customer pricing, discount policy, and margin by customer or product line. Individual employee compensation and the detailed organizational chart. Full board minutes and board materials. Source code, repository access, and anything approaching a code escrow. Penetration test findings and the open-vulnerability remediation log. Employee and contractor personnel files. Legal claim files, threatened litigation, and privileged counsel memoranda.


Those items specifically, because customer names, per-customer pricing, and individual compensation are the three categories a competitor could act on directly. Detailed org charts and comp data create recruiting and negotiation exposure before a deal is certain. Anonymizing customer identities lets Tier 2 carry real concentration analysis with customers labeled Customer A through Customer J, which is usually enough to assess the business.


One rule overrides all of it. Withhold competitive intelligence, never withhold a problem. A concentration risk or a missing 83(b) disclosed by you in a dated memo is a negotiation. The same fact discovered by an associate in week three is a repricing. The[fundraising guide](https://www.indinero.com/resources/fundraising-ebook/) walks through how that disclosure sequencing plays out across a process.


## How Indinero prepares the financial half of a data room


Four of the six folders on this checklist are maintained artifacts, not assembled ones. They either exist on the day an investor asks, or they get reconstructed under a term sheet clock.


Financial statements, tax filings, the reconciliations behind both, and the supporting schedules in the people folder are the four. Reconstruction is also where the two most expensive gaps on this page come from. Accrual conversion runs four to eight weeks. ## Frequently asked questions


A data room build raises the same handful of questions every time, usually about timing, tooling, and how much to show before a term sheet is signed. Here’s what founders and finance leads ask most often.


### How long does it take to build an investor data room?


Plan four to six weeks to build an investor data room before outreach, not the week a term sheet arrives. The longest-lead items set that window, not assembly effort. Converting cash-basis books to three years of accrual statements under ASC 606 runs four to eight weeks, a fresh 409A needs an appraisal plus board ratification, and a missing state payroll account moves at agency speed. At indinero the monthly close produces those accrual statements year-round, so the financial folders stay current instead of being reconstructed.


### Should I use a virtual data room tool or a shared drive?


Use a virtual data room tool for a priced round, because a shared drive can’t do per-investor permissions, dynamic watermarking, or instant revocation. Purpose-built platforms give every fund its own named user account and control access down to the individual document, with view-only defaults in the sensitive tiers and download allowed on the model. They also log views, downloads, and access location, and they let you expire documents or revoke a passed fund’s access the same week.


### Does a seed-stage startup need a data room at all?


A seed-stage startup needs a small data room, roughly 12 to 20 files, not the 45 to 70 a Series A requires. At seed, the core set is the deck, the cap table, historical P&L and burn, usage data covering growth and retention, and LTV to CAC with a payback period, plus incorporation documents. Series B and later adds reviewed or audited statements, a SOC 2 Type 2 report, and multi-state registration evidence by state.


### Which financial statements do investors expect to find in the room?


Investors expect three fiscal years of GAAP accrual income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements, plus year to date, monthly and annual. The trial balance and general ledger cover the same period, with trailing 12 months of reconciliations and a deferred revenue waterfall reconciling bookings to billings to GAAP revenue. Label the assurance level honestly, since most Series A rounds accept management-prepared statements. Indinero bundles bookkeeping, accounting, tax, and fractional CFO advisory in one monthly engagement, so the close produces these statements as standing artifacts.


### Should the cap table go in before I have a term sheet?


The cap table belongs in the first open tier of the data room, well before a term sheet, because investors read it first. Before modeling your business, a fund models its own ownership, so the cap table decides whether the round math works after the pool refresh and how the SAFE and note stack converts. A cap table summary is what the first tier needs. Individual employee compensation and full board minutes wait until a term sheet is signed.


### What happens if a document is missing once diligence starts?


A document missing from the data room turns every later file into a search for more gaps, so disclose the gap yourself. A fact you disclose is a negotiation. The same fact found by an associate in week three is a repricing. A missed 83(b) election has a 30-day window with no extensions and no equitable exceptions, so the only response is accurate disclosure and a tax analysis for the affected holder.


### Who on the team should control data room access?


One person should own data room access, usually the founder running the raise or the finance lead, and every fund gets a named account. Never a shared link and never a shared password, because named accounts are what make the activity log mean anything. That log is a sales instrument, not only a compliance record, since views, downloads, and time on page show which funds are doing real work. The same owner revokes access the week a process goes dead.
